name: Decoupled Pages
description: Provides a quick & easy way to create routes serving SPAs.
project_description: Decoupled Pages provides a quick and simple way to define new Drupal routes which can be overtaken by a single-page application (SPA), commonly written in JavaScript with React, Vue.js, Ember, or similar frameworks. Rather than writing a controller, a developer declares a normal route in a module's *.routing.yml and adds a `_decoupled_page_main` route default whose value is an asset library ID (e.g. `your_module/app`). The module's routing event subscriber validates the definition and swaps in its own internal controller, which renders an empty `<div id="decoupled-page-root">` inside the active theme's main content region and attaches the named library so the SPA can mount onto that element. Additional CSS/JS libraries can be attached with the `_decoupled_page_assets` route option, additional in-app deep-link paths can be registered with `_decoupled_page_paths` (each cloned into its own route that serves the same shell), and backend-to-frontend configuration can be passed as HTML `data-*` attributes on the root element via the `_decoupled_page_data` route default (static values) or a custom data provider service (dynamic values, e.g. derived from the request). Data attribute names are validated to lower-case letters and dashes; attribute values are rendered through Drupal's attribute system. The module intentionally does not manage route access: access is whatever the route's own `requirements` declare, and the SPA's data access (typically JSON:API or REST) is governed separately. It ships a `decoupled_pages_test` example/test submodule demonstrating static data, extra assets, additional paths, and a dynamic data provider.
